articles.headline: Brendan Carr says he’ll let Pete Hegseth decide whether TV networks can air the public execution
keyFacts: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr stated he will defer to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth on whether TV networks can broadcast the execution of Nidal Hasan.
The Pentagon plans to livestream the execution by firing squad, which may place it outside FCC jurisdiction on online platforms.
Major tech companies have not yet responded to inquiries regarding whether they will permit the execution livestream on their platforms.
body: FCC chairman Brendan Carr said he will defer to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth on whether TV networks can air the planned execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan by firing squad.
Brendan Carr says he’ll let Pete Hegseth decide whether TV networks can air the public execution
The Pentagon is planning to livestream the execution of a convicted shooter, but the FCC Chairman says that the agency will ‘defer to Secretary Hegseth’ about if it will be broadcast.

The Pentagon has said the execution will be livestreamed, suggesting it’ll appear on an online platform beyond the FCC’s jurisdiction. But it’s common for broadcast TV networks to air live video of government events, and Carr’s agency does have a say over what happens on public airwaves.

“My understanding is it’s not on broadcast TV, so I don’t think there’s a role for the FCC one way or the other,” Carr said in a CNBC interview today. “But I trust Secretary Hegseth. He’s implemented the laws and the regulations that are relevant to the Department of War, and I think he’s doing a great job, and I trust that he’s making the right call on these issues.”

When asked if the execution would be allowed on broadcast TV if the Defense Department wanted it, Carr said it would be Hegseth’s choice. “Ultimately we’re going to defer to Secretary Hegseth and his decisions on how to move forward with this,” Carr said.

The Verge has asked major tech companies whether they will allow the execution livestream on their platforms. As of this writing, YouTube, Twitch, Meta, and X haven’t responded to requests for comment.

articles.headline: Former College Basketball Star Heidi Burge Horton, Who Inspired Disney’s “Double Teamed”, Dies at 54
keyFacts: Former college basketball star Heidi Burge Horton died at the age of 54, the University of Virginia announced.
Horton and her twin sister played for the University of Virginia and inspired the 2002 Disney movie Double Teamed.
Horton died following a battle with grade four glioblastoma, a rapidly growing brain tumor.
body: Heidi Horton
Credit: Craig Jones/Allsport/Getty NEED TO KNOW
Former college basketball star Heidi Burge Horton has died at 54
Horton played for the University of Virginia with her twin sister, Heather, before later joining the WNBA
The twin sisters’ basketball careers inspired the 2002 Disney Channel movie Double Teamed
Heidi Burge Horton, a former standout college basketball player whose life and career playing with her twin sister inspired the Disney Channel movie Double Teamed , has died at 54.
Horton’s death was announced by the University of Virginia, her alma mater, on social media Thursday, Oct. 8.

“We are deeply saddened by the passing of Heidi Burge Horton,” the university’s women’s basketball program wrote. “Heidi was a cherished member of the Virginia Women’s Basketball family, her legacy will forever be a part of Virginia Athletics. Our sincere condolences to her family and loved ones.”

Horton and her twin sister, Heather, played for the Lady Cavaliers from 1989 and 1993. They helped lead the team to three Atlantic Coast Conference championships and three straight Final Four appearances in 1991, 1992 and 1993. Virginia lost the 1992 NCAA women’s basketball national championship game in overtime to the University of Tennessee.
Heidi Burge Horton
Credit: Todd Warshaw /Allsport Born in Harbor City, Calif., Horton and her sister played high school basketball together before accepting scholarships to join the Lady Cavaliers in 1987.

A 1993 Sports Illustrated story about a number of twins playing college basketball at the time described Heidi and Heather as opposites – Heidi playing a more defensive, rebounding role, while her sister was the team’s top point scorer.

The twins would “often argue,” according to the feature, but their combination on the court was undeniable, as the team experienced its most successful era to date with Horton, her sister, and their teammate, future six-time WNBA All-Star Dawn Staley, on the court.

After college, Horton played three seasons overseas before returning to the United States to join the WNBA in 1997, where she played two more professional seasons — her first with the Los Angeles Sparks and her last with the Washington Mystics.
Heidi Burge Horton
Credit: Andreas Rentz/Bongarts/Getty Horton retired from basketball following a back injury in 2000, according to local WTVR .
Two years later, Disney released Double Teamed , an original film inspired by Heidi and Heather that followed the twins’ rise in the sport.

An obituary for Horton says the former basketball star was diagnosed with grade four glioblastoma, a rapidly growing brain tumor, in October 2025. Her cancer went into remission following chemotherapy treatments but returned in July.
Horton is survived by her husband, Patrick Horton, and their two children: Jonathan, 23, and Holly, 21.

articles.headline: Pacers' Tyrese Haliburton reveals surprising weight gain after injury
keyFacts: Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton revealed on 'The Pat McAfee Show' that he intentionally gained 25 pounds while recovering from a torn Achilles.
Haliburton stated he now weighs 200 pounds compared to his previous weight of 175 pounds during the 2025 NBA Finals.
Haliburton plans to maintain his new 200-pound playing weight throughout the entire 2026-27 NBA season.
body: Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton is fully healthy nearly 16 months after tearing his Achilles during Game 7 of the NBA Finals, but he might look a bit different this season.
Speaking on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Thursday, Haliburton revealed he has undergone some changes since the injury, including adding more weight during the year off.
For Haliburton, that weight gain was intentional, with the hope that it makes a difference for him as he returns to the court.
Here's what you need to know about Haliburton's new playing weight.
Tyrese Haliburton reveals surprising weight gain

Haliburton revealed Thursday that he now weighs 200 pounds, which is 25 pounds heavier than he claims he was during the 2025 NBA Finals. That weight gain was intentional: the Indiana guard said he added muscle and bulked up during his season away from the court while rehabbing a torn Achilles.
Haliburton is listed at 185 pounds, but he claims he was closer to 175 before the devastating Achilles injury. He now plans to stay at 200 pounds for the entire 2026-27 season.

Tyrese Haliburton reveals he currently weighs 25 more pounds than he did in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals Haliburton added significant muscle and says he plans to play all season at 200 pounds (Via @PatMcAfeeShow) https://t.co/IphWCktH1D
— Fullcourtpass (@Fullcourtpass) October 8, 2026

While he's added muscle during the recovery process, Haliburton also faced a setback in early 2026 when he contracted shingles. The illness led to unintentional weight gain due to medication, along with other symptoms.

"I’ve been taking unbelievable amounts of medication to try to get rid of it. It hasn’t worked," Haliburton told reporters in April. "It’s obviously caused me to gain weight. That’s been a topic of conversation through social media."
That led to some concern about Haliburton's appearance, but the Pacers star is making it clear he's intentionally bulked up and hopes a larger frame helps him return to form this season.

articles.headline: Leisure Suit Larry is about to take his final bow
keyFacts: Publisher Assemble Entertainment announced that Leisure Suit Larry: Wet Dreams Don't Dry and Wet Dreams Dry Twice will be removed from Steam on October 23.
The publisher did not provide a reason for the delisting or comment on whether the games will eventually return.
Both games are currently available at a 95% discount for less than $2 each ahead of their removal.
body: 2018's Leisure Suit Larry: Wet Dreams Don't Dry was a genuinely pleasant surprise, in that it's actually good—quite a contrast to the preceding games in the series, Magna Cum Laude and Box Office Bust, which were decidedly not good. A sequel followed, Wet Dreams Dry Twice, and once again it was pretty good stuff—not hugely innovative or high art, but a genuine Leisure Suit Larry experience that manages to avoid embarrassing itself (though it embarrasses Larry himself plenty).

Both of them, sadly, are soon going away for good. An announcement on Steam from publisher Assemble Entertainment says both games are being removed from the store on October 23. Ahead of that, they're being offered seriously cheap: 95% off the regular price, dropping them to less than $2 each.
The removal of the Wet Dreams duo effectively puts a pin in a process than began in 2025, when the OG Larry games were removed from sale:
- Leisure Suit Larry – Magna Cum Laude Uncut and Uncensored
- Leisure Suit Larry 1 – In the Land of the Lounge Lizards
- Leisure Suit Larry 2 – Looking For Love (In Several Wrong Places)
- Leisure Suit Larry 3 – Passionate Patti in Pursuit of the Pulsating Pectorals
- Leisure Suit Larry 5 – Passionate Patti Does a Little Undercover Work
- Leisure Suit Larry 6 – Shape Up Or Slip Out
- Leisure Suit Larry 7 – Love for Sail
Leisure Suit Larry 4 managed to avoid the executioner's axe by not existing in the first place.

A reason for this new round of delistings wasn't provided, nor did Assemble comment on the possibility of an eventual return. Expiring licenses rights are a common culprit for this sort of thing, and that seems to be a good bet here: Leisure Suit Larry was originally a Sierra game, which I assume means Assemble licensed the property from Activision for the Wet Dreams duo; given the timing (Wet Dreams Don't Dry was announced in 2018), we're coming up on roughly 10 years since that deal would've been done, which, as someone who's bad at math and thus likes nice round numbers, seems to me like a reasonably possible expiration date for such a deal.

But that's entirely speculation. What's certain is that Leisure Suit Larry: Wet Dreams Don't Dry and Wet Dreams Dry Twice are going away for good, and ahead of that they're both really cheap on both Steam and GOG—the delisting announcement makes no mention of their fate on GOG but it's a safe assumption they'll be disappeared there, too—until they're gone. Get 'em while they're wet.

- Leisure Suit Larry: Wet Dreams Dry Twice: Steam, GOG

articles.headline: Scalpers from the US are not the only players looking to score a piece of the .si domain gold rush — but the country dominating the list might surprise you
keyFacts: Register.si logged 19,541 new .si domain registrations in a 24-hour period ending October 9, 2026, driven by a US executive order rebranding artificial intelligence as super intelligence.
Data from Hostinger showed that customers in India registered 3,174 .si names, slightly edging out the US at 3,135, while Morocco ranked third with 678 registrations.
Netcraft found that many newly registered .si domains were promptly listed on resale marketplaces, raising questions about whether the domains will survive their first renewal in late 2027.
body: - Register.si logged 19,541 new .si names in 24 hours, about five times its pre-order daily pace
- India (3,174) edged the US (3,135) in Hostinger's data, with Morocco a surprising third on 678
- Hostinger handled roughly two in five new .si names on September 30 and October 1 2026, and says its sales peaked October 5 before cooling to about 4x pre-order levels
The scramble for Slovenia's .si domain has not burned out just yet: on October 9 2026, the live counter on the Register.si homepage showed 19,541 new .si names registered in the preceding 24 hours.
This is roughly five times the average of about 3,700 a day the registry logged in the week between President Trump's UN speech and his executive order.

The usual assumption would be that this is an American land grab of virtual real estate, but data from Hostinger, one of the biggest retail sellers of the extension, complicates that picture considerably: across the nine days its dashboard covers, customers in India registered 3,174 .si names against 3,135 from the US, a gap of just 39 even as Morocco comes a distant third.
A domain rush concentrated on short names
The gold rush started at the UN General Assembly on September 22 2026, where President Trump said the US government would start calling AI "super intelligence," or SI.

A week later, he signed Executive Order 14434, "Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence," which tells federal agencies to swap in the new terms and says the executive branch "will not acknowledge the use of 'Artificial Intelligence' and 'AI.'"

That label happens to match Slovenia's country code, in use since 1992; anyone can register a .si name without a Slovenian address, and it can be bought for a single year, while Anguilla's .ai requires a two-year minimum.
With a much lower barrier to entry, scalpers and opportunists alike have flooded in, targeting domain names across the board, most aiming for a quick flip if the .si domain name catches on.

The registry's own numbers show how fast things moved. Register.si recorded 3,515 new .si domains in all of August and 46,066 in September, about 13 times as many. Its daily chart, as seen on XenoSpectrum, shows 4,115 registrations on September 29, the day the order was signed, then 11,331 on September 30 and 12,728 on October 1.
A domain rush concentrated on short names and a surprising number of Indian buyers

Hostinger's country table, which it shared exclusively with TechRadar Pro, is where the story gets interesting. India accounted for 25.5% (3,174) of its .si registrations and the US for 25.2% (3,135), together just over half, matching what the company told TechCrunch.
Morocco followed at a distant 3rd with 678, ahead of the UK (425), Canada (409), Germany (374) and the UAE (363). Pakistan ranked eighth with 260, and Egypt and Algeria also made the top 20.

What buyers are choosing is just as revealing. Hostinger could not classify 57.1% of the names. Among the rest, short names led with 1,554, followed by tech-themed names at 1,040 and explicitly AI-themed names at 372.

That is a ratio of about 4.2 to 1 in favor of short names, and AI names made up only 3% of all .si registrations in the period. US buyers followed the same pattern, with short names their top category at 306.

Plenty of evidence points to speculation; Netcraft found that just over half of the .si names it saw registered at Dynadot between Trump's Truth Social poll and his UN speech were promptly listed on Dynadot's resale marketplace.
It also found 87 .com names pairing household brands with "superintelligence," registered hours before the order was signed and listed at $20,000 each, though it saw no evidence any had sold.

Names like build.si carry seven-figure asking prices, and of 35 publicly documented .si sales in the first half of 2026, only two went to companies that actually use the domain, including AI startup Recursive, which paid $20,000 for recursive.si.

The problem (or rather the opportunity) isn't really a problem: registration is cheap. Hostinger charges $11.99 for the first year and $16.99 to renew, and Register.si takes €10 per domain. This allows anyone with $1200 to spare (sans any coupon discounts they might be able to find) to essentially be able to hoard, squat, or scalp, depending on the terminology one prefers, as many as 100 domains without much to worry about.

Domain Name Wire estimated the September surge brought the registry around €300,000 in extra revenue, arguably chump change next to the roughly $85.3 million Anguilla earned from .ai in 2025, per CircleID.

The real question is how many of these names survive their first renewal in late 2027. If "SI" stays a White House term while the rest of the industry keeps saying AI, a large share of this year's speculative registrations will quietly lapse. The 60-day deadline for a formal federal definition could reshape that calculation either way, even as the Trump administration remains adamant that the change will be increasingly visible in the days to come.

articles.headline: Vikings Creator’s New Series Bloodaxe Sets 2027 Premiere Date
keyFacts: Vikings creator Michael Hirst announced that his new historical action series Bloodaxe will premiere on Prime Video on January 20, 2027.
The eight-episode first season follows the 10th-century rise of Norse raider Erik Bloodaxe and his wife Gunnhild amid political power struggles.
Bloodaxe has already secured a second season that is currently in production in Ireland.
body: Fans of Netflix's Vikings have a new Norse saga to look forward to. Bloodaxe, the upcoming historical action series from Vikings creator Michael Hirst, will premiere on Prime Video on Jan. 20, 2027.

The series debuted its first teaser trailer Friday during a panel at New York Comic Con, where Hirst, co-showrunner Horatio Hirst, and cast members Xavier Molyneux, Jessica Madsen, and Levi Miller discussed the show. All eight episodes of Bloodaxe season 1 will arrive on the same day.
What is Bloodaxe about?

Set in 10th-century Norway, Bloodaxe follows the rise of Erik Bloodaxe (Molyneux), a Norse raider fighting to claim the Norwegian throne alongside his wife, Gunnhild, Mother of Kings (Madsen). Their quest unfolds amid rivalries, shifting alliances, and bloody betrayals, with rulers from across Scandinavia — and a powerful English king — drawn into the conflict.

Like Vikings, Hirst’s new series draws on the history and legends of the Norse world, with political power struggles and violent clashes at the center of its story. Hirst created the original Vikings series, which ran for six seasons on Netflix, from 2013 to 2020. Hirst later served as an executive producer on its sequel, Vikings: Valhalla.

Bloodaxe has already secured a second season, which is currently in production in Ireland. The series also stars Karlis Arnolds Avots, Rod Hallett, Alina Tomnikov, Sisse Marie, Rune Temte, and Jesper Christensen.
Bloodaxe premieres Jan. 20, 2027, exclusively on Prime Video.

articles.headline: Gears of War: E-Day is struggling with sales, giving another argument to day one Game Pass haters
keyFacts: Alinea Analytics reported that Gears of War: E-Day sold 230,000 copies and generated $37 million overall.
Matt Piscatella reported that Xbox hardware sales dropped by 33 percent recently in the lead-up to the game.
Destructoid reported that the game's lower direct sales raise questions about the viability of day-one Game Pass releases.
body: Gears of War: E-Day is, by all accounts, a great game. Reviewers loved it, praised its quality of gameplay and story and graphics alike, and the players seem very fond of what it was trying to do. Whichever way you cut it, E-Day was meant to be a stellar box office success. But it is not, begging the question: is it time for day one Game Pass to go?

According to Alinea Analytics , Gears of War E-Day sold just 230,000 copies, generating $37 million overall. However, around 950,000 people paid something to get into E-Day , including 722,000 players who dished out an extra $30 to access the game early via its Premium Edition. This includes a significant number of players who played the game through Game Pass, but it still leaves the title at around $58 million generated since launch, with the numbers rapidly mellowing out and plateauing.
Image via Xbox Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter !

To put it in perspective, Alinea Analytics says that if 75 percent of these upgrades simply bought the game, it would’ve generated double the amount. Instead, they just paid what they would’ve already paid for Game Pass, with a little extra sprinkled on top. About 90 percent of Gears players also played CoD , and I’m willing to bet they’re buying the thing at full price while staying subscribed to Game Pass.

We could argue that with Gears now part of the subscription, more people are keen on getting it, or perhaps even willing to buy an Xbox for it. However, Xbox hardware sales have dropped another 33 percent recently ( via Matt Piscatella ), so in the lead-up to the game, people did not seem super interested in spending a good sum just to play this new exclusive, especially since it’s also on PC and, again, on day one Game Pass.

Image via Xbox As Alinea Analytics indicates, a game with such rave reviews and a fantastic response from the community should, by all metrics, do well. And so many games out there do perform quite well on Steam and third-party platforms despite day-one Game Pass availability, so there seems to also be a factor of uncertainty playing a major role in Microsoft’s inability to put out a sweeping first-party title.

A game of this caliber should not be offered as a bonus. What happens is that poor sales lead to layoffs and cancellations when they otherwise would’ve incentivized further development in that area, so it might be high time to cancel the one thing causing all the trouble.

articles.headline: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson for Week 5 matchup vs. Falcons due to ankle injury
keyFacts: The Baltimore Ravens ruled out quarterback Lamar Jackson for their Week 5 game against the Atlanta Falcons due to an ankle injury.
Tyler Huntley will start at quarterback for Baltimore in place of Jackson, who did not practice all week.
Jackson injured his ankle during the second quarter of the Ravens' win over the Tennessee Titans last Sunday.
body: The Baltimore Ravens will be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson when the team travels to Atlanta to take on the red-hot Falcons, as he has been ruled out with an ankle injury. Tyler Huntley will start under center as Baltimore looks to improve on its 3-1 record.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters they knew Jackson being ruled out for Week 5 was always a possibility, but that the quarterback worked "his tail off" in recovery, and is "doing everything in his power to get back." He did not practice at all this week.

The two-time NFL MVP injured his ankle at the end of the second quarter in the Ravens' eventual 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans last Sunday. On the second-to-last play of the first half, Jermaine Johnson II tackled Jackson, who appeared to twist his ankle. Jackson was having an impressive game up to that point, completing 15-of-20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns.

Huntley replaced Jackson in the third quarter and completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards and rushed four times for 16 yards. The Ravens did not score a single point in the final two quarters. "Snoop" has a 7-9 record as a starter and has scored 14 total touchdowns compared to 12 turnovers.

The Ravens are 6-11 in the regular season without Jackson since he became the full-time starter. His durability has become a talking point, as Baltimore has won zero playoff games in seasons where Jackson missed time due to injuries.

Jackson's injury comes at a bad time, as the Ravens have to travel to take on one of the hottest teams in the NFL in prime time. Since Michael Penix Jr. returned to the field, the Falcons are averaging 40.0 points per game after averaging just 8.0 points per game in Weeks 1-2. Penix has brought some stability to the passing attack, as Drake London is averaging 145.0 receiving yards per game over the past two contests, but the real headliner for Atlanta's offense is running back Bijan Robinson.

Robinson ranks second in rushing yards per game (123.5) and scrimmage yards per game (153.5) entering Week 5. In the Falcons' 45-24 shellacking of the New Orleans Saints on Monday night, he rushed for 145 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries. Brian Robinson Jr. also played a part in the beatdown, rushing for 62 yards and three touchdowns. The Falcons ran 35 times and passed the ball just 20 times. The Falcons also boast the No. 1 rushing defense in the league, allowing 48.3 rushing yards per game.

articles.headline: Michael van Gerwen told he doesn’t deserve Premier League spot amid nightmare season
keyFacts: Vincent van der Voort said Michael van Gerwen does not deserve a 2027 Premier League spot due to poor form in 2026.
Van der Voort suggested that skipping the Premier League could help Van Gerwen focus on his ranking.
Van der Voort also stated that Wessel Nijman should not be selected for the Premier League because he lacks success in televised events.
body: Michael van Gerwen shouldn’t be in the 2027 Premier League – and should reject an invite if it comes his way.
Thats the view of ex-PDC star and the Dutchman’s close friend Vincent van der Voort, who has commented on MVG’s poor form in 2026.
Van Gerwen is yet to reach a PDC quarter-final in 2026, with the Dutchman falling to ninth in the rankings Getty
The three-time champion of the world’s struggles were compounded by a first-round exit in the World Grand Prix of Darts .
And his performances in the big televised events have been well below par – winning just one night in the Premier League this year.
He also didn’t make it to Finals Night, and there is a possibility that he drops out of the top 16 by the end of the year, with a lot resting on how he performs at the PDC World Darts Championship .
But Van der Voort thinks a rest from the Premier League might actually be a good thing for Van Gerwen .
What has been said about Van Gerwen’s form?
Speaking to Online Darts, he said: “Of course, if you look at what he has done for the sport and everything, he should be in.
“But if you judge it on this year until now, he shouldn’t.
“First round in the Masters, last 16 at the UK Open, early exit at the Matchplay and then losing here in the first round. You can’t say he deserves to be in based on that.

“Maybe for his career it would actually be better not to play it. Commercially and money-wise, of course, it is a lot of money, but for everything else, the best thing might be to skip it and fully focus on his ranking.”
And Van der Voort doesn’t think another fellow Dutchman – Wessel Nijman – should be in the Premier League either.
The 26-year-old sits in 12th place in the PDC’s Order of Merit, having won six Players Championship titles, while winning twice on the European Tour.
Van Gerwen has won just one PDC major since 2023 Getty
Nijman has won eight titles in 2026, but has struggled in televised events Getty
But he is yet to go beyond the fifth round of a televised event in 2026.
And for that reason, Van der Voort doesn’t think Nijman would be a wise choice for Premier League selection.
He remarked: “At this moment, it’s too early. He hasn’t shown it on the big stage.

“The Premier League should be a place for people who have done well on TV. They then get something extra commercially and everything. But Wessel hasn’t been in the quarter-finals of a TV tournament yet.
“Maybe this weekend will be his weekend, and then he has to play well in all the other tournaments. But for now, it’s not.
“You can’t say to a player who has never been in a semi-final or final of a TV tournament, ‘You’re a Premier League player,’ that’s what I think.”

articles.headline: Maryland’s GOP governor nominee ‘not pursuing’ Trump’s backing in race against Wes Moore
keyFacts: Maryland Republican gubernatorial nominee Dan Cox stated he is not pursuing President Donald Trump's endorsement for his campaign against Governor Wes Moore.
Cox acknowledged that Republicans must adapt to win in Maryland, working with former Governor Robert Ehrlich to rebuild a broader coalition.
Cox faces significant challenges against Moore, a Democratic incumbent who leads significantly in polls and has faced criticism for dodging questions about his term.
body: Maryland Republican gubernatorial nominee Dan Cox isn’t courting President Donald Trump’s support in his second campaign against Gov. Wes Moore (D-MD), despite the conservative former firebrand state lawmaker being warmly embraced by the president in 2022.

Cox, in a nod to The Old Line State’s blue voting tendencies and a symbol of how he’s moderated some of his more extreme election fraud rhetoric from his first go-around, acknowledged Republicans across the map “have to be smart to win.”

“No conversations, and I’m not pursuing that,” Cox told the Washington Examiner in an interview Friday about talks with anyone in Trump’s orbit or the desire for an endorsement. “It’s important that the president continue his role of serving the nation, and getting involved in endorsing a candidate for office in Maryland, I don’t think it is something that would be helpful to — well, I wouldn’t say helpful. I don’t think that would be something that is within the importance of his work.”

His comments came just days after Trump spoke at a Baltimore shipyard Tuesday as part of an official visit to tout a new public-private project with the Navy to expand U.S. submarine production and defense manufacturing.
“He came to Maryland the other day and did exactly what he has been doing across the nation, and that is trying to bring economic boost,” Cox said.

The former Maryland delegate lost to Moore in 2022 by more than 32 points in a race to succeed the term-limited centrist Republican governor, Larry Hogan . Trump’s endorsement catapulted Cox from a long-shot underdog to primary winner against Hogan Cabinet member Kelly Schulz. Hogan was a staunch Trump opponent.

But in a state Trump lost by nearly 29 points to former Vice President Kamala Harris, and with the GOP facing midterm headwinds from voters’ affordability anxieties, Cox’s mindset has evolved. Former Maryland Gov. Robert Ehrlich, who served from 2003-2007 and branded himself as a right-of-center Republican, serves as Cox’s campaign finance adviser and is among those he said who are helping him make a broader appeal.

“I think the approach that the president made clear to Republicans everywhere, as leader of our party, is that we have to be smart to win,” Cox said. “I am working hard with Governor Ehrlich as my finance chair to rebuild the, what I would call the Ehrlich-Hogan coalition across Maryland and to strengthen that common sense economic approach.”
Dan Cox, Republican gubernatorial candidate in Maryland, speaks during a campaign results reception, Tuesday, Nov. 8, 2022, in Annapolis, Md. (AP Photo/Steve Ruark)

Cox has not spoken with Hogan, who was critical of his 2022 candidacy and stolen 2020 election claims that mirrored those of Trump and his allies. He noted that he has “members of [Hogan’s] Cabinet helping me and advising me,” and praised Hogan’s tenure handling economic issues.
WES MOORE’S 2028 DODGE COMPLICATES REELECTION PITCH IN MARYLAND

Still, Cox faces long-shot — if not insurmountable — odds against Moore, a Democratic figure with national name identification who leads by a 2:1 margin in the polls and is widely expected to run for president in 2028. The first-term governor refused to rule out leaving office early during their debate this week, and he’s spent much of his time in office traversing the country to campaign for battleground candidates. Moore has previously denied he’s weighing a White House bid.

“If you’re standing for governor and not willing to serve as governor, why would you vote for that person? I think it’s a travesty,” Cox said of Moore’s dodge on the debate stage for serving a full second term. “Let’s bring the lieutenant governor on stage then, because I need to debate the person who wants to be governor.”

articles.headline: Nobel Peace Prize awarded to former ICC judge Navi Pillay

body: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 was awarded Friday to Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, a South African-born former judge with the International Criminal Court who went on to become the United Nations human rights chief and is still serving with the U.N.'s other judicial body, the International Court of Justice. She also led a U.N. inquiry last year that accused Israel of genocide in the Gaza Strip, and Israel was quick to condemn her receiving the honor on Friday.

The Nobel Committee said it was honoring Pillay "for her efforts to promote peace and international law," and that awarding the prize to someone with her body of work on international justice was a message to those seeking to undermine international law institutions.

The South African-born former United Nations human rights chief, who is 85, was recognized for her efforts to promote peace and international law, said Jørgen Watne Frydnes, chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee.
"This is definitely a message to those who are undermining the international system and institutions," Frydnes said.

"The system of international law is under tremendous pressure and its institutions are under attack," he said, noting what the committee saw as a shift "towards power politics at the expense of legal frameworks and global respect for law and justice."

The International Criminal Court (ICC) has come under fire from Israel and the Trump administration in recent years, with the U.S. imposing sanctions against the U.N. court last year after it in 2024 for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. President Trump accused the court of "illegitimate and baseless actions targeting America and our close ally Israel."
The against its staff and said they were intended to "harm (the Court's) independent and impartial judicial work."

Pillay served as an ICC judge from 2003 until 2008, when she resigned to take on the role of United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. She was the chair of the U.N. Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory that said last year it had . Israel dismissed the report as "scandalous."

Pillay is currently serving as an ad hoc judge for the International Court of Justice (ICJ), which is separate to the ICC, in the case of Gambia v. Myanmar, in which Myanmar's ruling military junta stands accused of genocide over its in the western state of Rakhine.

Frydnes said the committee wasn't immediately able to reach Pillay Friday to tell her she had been awarded the prize, adding from the podium that if she was watching and saw a call coming in from a Norwegian phone number, to "please pick up."

She soon appeared in a video posted on social media by the head of Amnesty International, being applauded by well-wishers at the Palace of Justice in Nuremberg, Germany, where Nazi leaders were put on trial for their crimes against humanity after World War II.

"Perhaps it was meant to be that I was in this historic courtroom... when the announcement was made and I was informed of the award," Pillay said. "We are living through an era when international law and human rights are under significant political attack ... This worsening reality is particularly visible with the attacks on the International Criminal Court."

"If you clap a little bit louder I may share this prize with Trump," she quipped, drawing laughs from the crowd. She said that when she was informed that she had been awarded the prize, she first thought "it must be a joke," and that as a "lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this thing."

She noted that she was lauded by the Nobel committee for her courage, which she questioned, saying: "You can imagine how surprised I was. Why would you need courage to speak the truth? You interpret the law, you look at all the facts, so it's an impartial decision you make."
Israel condemns Pillay's honor, U.S. further sanctions ICC

The Israeli Foreign Ministry blasted the Nobel committee for awarding the prize to Pillay on Friday, saying in a statement posted online that "if there were an award for lies, hatred, and blood libels, Navi Pillay wouldn't just be a contender. She'd be a frontrunner. Her role in the relentless, politically motivated demonization of Israel and promotion of the genoLIE speaks volumes."
It condemned the committee for awarding her as "the grotesque weaponization of an award to legitimize anti-Israel hatred and prejudice."

A separate statement posted on the X account of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the Nobel committee had "lost its moral compass. It has awarded its highest honor to a bigot who built her career around inventing and propagating blood libels against the one and only Jewish state."

The Trump administration, hours later, announced further sanctions against the ICC. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the ICC a "threat to U.S. sovereignty" and said the new measures were deemed necessary to ensure the court, which the U.S. has never been a state party to, can never prosecute a U.S. national.

He said the new sanctions would "ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate," adding: "We expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American servicemembers for their defense, to rein in the court. If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC, brick by brick, until Americans are threatened no longer."

The ICC has never prosecuted or indicted a U.S. national, but it has investigated the actions of U.S. forces abroad, in countries where it does have jurisdiction, including Afghanistan, and it could theoretically seek to prosecute Americans.

According to Human Rights Watch, there are "limited situations in which the ICC has jurisdiction over the nationals of countries, such as the U.S., that have not joined the Rome Statute. This includes when a citizen of a non-member country commits war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide on the territory of an ICC member country. That's why U.S. citizens may be subject to the court's jurisdiction as it investigates alleged grave crimes that took place in Afghanistan."
Nobel prize history

Last year, Venezuelan opposition leader the Nobel Peace Prize for her struggle to achieve a democratic transition in the South American nation, winning recognition as a woman "who keeps the flame of democracy burning amid a growing darkness."

Machado gave President Trump, who has long said he deserves the prize, her Nobel medal shortly after the United States ousted then-President Nicolás Maduro. But it was largely a symbolic gesture: The Nobel Committee has said the honor itself cannot be transferred.

Nominations can be made by a select group of people and organizations, including heads of state or politicians serving at a national level, university professors, directors of foreign policy institutes, past Nobel Prize recipients and members of the Norwegian Nobel Committee itself.

Four of this year's Nobels were announced earlier this week. The Nobel for medicine went to three scientists whose work led to a tool that uses light to help unravel how the brain works. The physics award recognized a scientist's efforts to demystify a rare group of neutrinos. The chemistry prize recognized two scientists for untangling mysterious mirror images in molecules, a discovery that has been used to develop countless drugs.
Canadian poet, essayist and translator Anne Carson won the literature prize Thursday for "bold and inventive" works that fuse the classical and the modern and blur the boundaries of poetry and prose.
The Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences will be announced Monday.
The prize money this year is 12 million Swedish kronor (about $1.2 million).
Education activist Malala Yousafzai is the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate; she won at 17 in 2014.

The United States is the most-credited country, with 24 awards naming U.S. institutions or individuals, ahead of the United Kingdom (13) and Switzerland (11). No laureate listed as American has won since then-President Barack Obama was awarded in 2009.

The prize has gone unawarded on 19 occasions, most of them during the world wars. In 1948, the year Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated, no prize was awarded; he had been nominated 12 times and never won.
In 1939, a Swedish member of parliament nominated Adolf Hitler, then withdrew the nomination, saying it was never meant seriously.

articles.headline: Rockstar HR Questioned Over Discord ‘Mole’ And Sudden Timing Of GTA 6 Dev Firings In Latest Labor Tribunal Hearing
keyFacts: An employment tribunal in Glasgow is hearing a dispute over whether Rockstar Games engaged in union busting by firing over 30 employees for gross misconduct.
Fired developers claim Rockstar targeted them to stop unionization, while HR director Charlie Kinloch testified that employees were fired to prevent sensitive leaks ahead of a major announcement.
The tribunal hearing will continue next week with testimony from additional Rockstar management witnesses.
body: A fight over allegations of union busting at Rockstar Games is currently underway at an employment tribunal in Glasgow, Scotland. The Grand Theft Auto 6 studio maintains that over 30 employees were fired last year for gross misconduct, including the leaking of sensitive information about the development of the upcoming game. The fired developers claim the Rockstar just wanted to prevent the UK trade group IWGB from getting a foothold at the company. The latest turn in the proceedings saw Rockstar Lincoln co-studio manager and HR director Charlie Kinloch questioned over one of the more surprising claims in the case: a junior employee who acted as a mole alleging spying on union activity in a separate Discord server.

Dueling sets of claims around this part of last fall’s firings were filed last month, and lawyers are now able to question witnesses related to the case about what happened. Among the claims is that someone under the alias “AB” was passing screenshots of union activity in the Discord server to Kinloch for over two years. This provided studio management with a shocking level of insight into what developers were saying when they thought no one was watching, remarks that would later be used to build a case for their firings. But Kinloch had access to this information for years. Why did it take until October of 2025 for Rockstar to act?

The fired developers contend that information was passed to Kinloch showing the group was just 12 members away–10 percent of the workforce–from the threshold needed to have a recognized union at Rockstar. But Kinloch contends that he never had any interest or knowledge of their union status, and was purely interested in limiting the risk to Rockstar from potential leaks. Here’s an excerpt from today’s questioning:

Lawyer: These comments, these posts on the Discord, which you knew about from March 2025 and June 2025 respectively, were not urgent concerns, which, sorry, they were not serious allegations, which urgently required further investigation to protect Rockstar’s interests, or you would have investigated them in March and June 2025?

Kinloch:Â It’s important for me to articulate the lens through which I viewed it, viewed these comments at that point, the point where we…in October…this was the point where the business was on the cusp, I later learned, of making a significant announcement about the development of our next project. And through that lens, discussions about working hours, and crunch, and matters to do with the way that the business worked, when viewed through that lens, were, to my mind, incredibly significant. Coupled with the fact that as we got to that point in the game’s development, media speculation, the public’s interest in the organization was at its absolute peak, where a single one of those comments, if it were to hit the public forum, would cause the company damage, would cause the company hurt, and would paint a picture of the next stages of GTA 6‘s development on the cusp of a major commercially sensitive announcement. That was the lens that I reviewed those comments through in October.

So what was the big announcement? Well, the unionizing developers were fired at the end of October. Just days later, Rockstar Games announced that GTA 6 would be delayed from May 2026 to November 2026. There was immediate speculation about whether there was any connection between the two events, and whether development delays were related to the desire among some developers to unionize. The lawyer representing the fired developers pushed Kinloch on the timing questing”

Lawyer: You say in your IR statement, paragraph 28, “Due to the urgent and serious threat to our business,” do you see that? “We had to act as quickly as possible.” Is 18 months as quickly as possible.”
Kinloch: If I can provide some broad explanation there…
Lawyer: If there’s something additional to what you said before about the situation of the business in October 2025 being different by all means.

Kinloch: So the situation was rather different at this moment. Because we had seen that the membership of the Discord was expanding at an exponential rate. And some, perhaps half or more of the people who were joining the Discord at this moment in October were people whose names we could not determine.Â It seemed that the brazenness of which people were commenting about internal processes or disparaging the company was increasing in line with the exponential growth of the membership of that Discord on the cusp of a very significant announcement [that the] business was about to make. That is the urgency I’m referring to at that time.
Lawyer: Did you say “the brazenness of the comments of the disparagement?”
Kinloch: Yes, seem to be increasing in line with the expansion of the numbers that were joining the Discord

Lawyer: It doesn’t get much more brazen than what we’re looking at there with Jacob Jones. He’s saying the too long don’t read is that I got bullied out by my former director. They’re failing to give me work from home due to my ASD and they’re not redeploying me. So it’s a straightforward allegation of facility discrimination, isn’t it?

Kinloch: Yes. And under the broader context of a period of time in Rockstar’s history where there was no forthcoming major announcements, no immediate development of what will be the biggest game in the history of video games. And looking at it through that lens, that information becomes somewhat less commercially problematic if it were to hit the public sphere. If we fast forward X amount of months, we reach a point where, in my view, the damage that could be caused by a comment such as that would be commercially sensitive and carry a financial incentive for someone to leak. What I mean by that is if someone had that information to hand as we run up to the release of GTA 6, they could make money from that. They could generate clicks from that and they could create a story from that. That would be commercial but commercially valuable to the person who takes the information reports on it and commercially damaging to the business at that critical juncture.

The studio manager goes on to discuss how the growing membership of the Discord server, full of names the company didn’t know, led to a rapid increase in the risk of damaging proprietary information getting out. There are conflicting claims about the security of the server. The fired employees maintain that users were kept siloed in different channels and identities were authenticated before people were admitted into the union discussion channels specifically. Rockstar, meanwhile, has claimed that at least one journalist was present in one of the channels, and closely guarded secrets like a mysterious “32 player format” were discussed at one point.

But one of the key witnesses as to Rockstar’s intent with monitoring the developer Discord server remains the secret “mole” referred to as “AB.” While Rockstar maintains that AB shared information with management about worker activities of their own volition, AB is not among the witnesses that will be allowed to be questioned during the hearing. At one point the lawyer for the fired developers argued with the judge about the need to get Kinloch or others at Rockstar on the record about AB’s intents and unwillingness to let the person speak for themselves in order to establish an “adverse inference” in support of its argument that Rockstar paid AB and others with “time off in lieu in exchange for spying on their colleagues’ union activity.”

The hearing will continue next week, and other witnesses in Rockstar management sound likely to be called to testify. GTA 6, meanwhile, is just over a month away from finally releasing. Fired employees have asked players not to boycott the game but to but to support their legal battle instead.

articles.headline: Trump establishes committee to investigate Fed governor Lisa Cook
keyFacts: Donald Trump announced a committee to investigate Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook over mortgage fraud allegations to decide if cause exists for removal.
Cook's lawyers stated the fraud claims stem from clerical errors, after the Supreme Court previously ruled her earlier firing by Trump was unconstitutional.
The White House will hold a closed hearing on November 5 where Cook can present evidence and face legal examination.
body: Donald Trump announced on Friday that he is establishing a committee to investigate Lisa Cook, the US Federal Reserve governor, over allegations that she committed mortgage fraud, renewing his efforts to oust her despite a June supreme court ruling that her earlier firing was unconstitutional.

Trump said a committee will consult with justice department officials to decide whether there is “cause” for her removal. The White House will hold an in-person hearing on 5 November to consider the allegations against Cook, which will be closed to the public but transcribed and published. Cook will be able to submit a written statement to present her own evidence and will be subject to examination from White House and her own legal counsel.

“As President, it is my job to ensure the laws are faithfully executed, including by firing subordinates who cannot be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law,” Trump said in a statement posted to the White House’s website.
Her legal team has maintained that the White House is “cherrypicking” facts and any claims of fraud are based on unrelated clerical errors.
In response to the announcement, Cook’s lawyers said that they had “grave doubts” that the White House hearing would be “a legitimate one that would conform to the law”.
“But if it is anything close to objective,” they continued, “the conclusion will be that Governor Cook did not commit mortgage fraud, leaving no cause to remove her from the Federal Reserve Board.”
They added that Cook “welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name and demonstrate there is no legal basis to fire her”.

Cook was appointed by Joe Biden in 2022 to a 14-year term, becoming the Fed’s first Black governor. Before her tenure at the central bank, she taught at Harvard University and Stanford University and served on Barack Obama’s council of economic advisers.

Cook’s battle with the White House began in August 2025 when she was abruptly fired after Trump said she committed mortgage fraud by listing two properties in Georgia and Michigan as her primary residence and failing to report rental income on her Atlanta property.
Cook immediately sued the Trump administration, and the supreme court reinstated her after a 5-4 ruling that she could stay on as governor while fighting the fraud allegations.
In June, the court ruled that Trump’s firing was unconstitutional because he did not follow proper procedure and give Cook an opportunity to dispute the allegations before she was fired.

Cook was fired just as Trump was launching unprecedented attacks on the Fed’s chair, then Jerome Powell, in his blustering push to get the central bank to lower interest rates. Trump also launched a justice department investigation into Powell, which was dropped in April.
Congress created the Fed to be an independent and non-partisan institution. Economists widely agree that a central bank unswayed by politics is essential for the stability of a country’s economy.

Kevin Warsh, Powell’s successor, has repeatedly faced questions over how he will maintain the Fed’s independence. Before Trump picked him to lead the world’s most powerful central bank, he had echoed the president’s calls for cutting rates. But because of elevated inflation brought on by the war in the Middle East, the bank ultimately voted to raise rates in its last meeting, which drew the ire of the White House just more than a month before the crucial midterm elections.

articles.headline: Gears of War: E-Day reportedly courts over 1.7m Xbox Game Pass players and makes over $37m since launch
keyFacts: Analyst Rhys Elliott reported that Gears of War: E-Day has attracted over 1.7 million Xbox Game Pass players and generated more than 37 million dollars since launch.
Elliott stated that Xbox sold roughly 230,000 standalone copies, while over 722,000 Game Pass subscribers purchased a 30-dollar Premium Edition upgrade.
Studio head Mike Crump said the game provides a strong foundation for future sequels that will take less time to develop.
body: Gears of War: E-Day's sales are reportedly lighter than you might expect from one of Xbox's flagship names, but pure sales numbers don't paint a complete picture of the bloody shooter's performance. A sizable chunk of revenue actually came from Game Pass subscribers paying for the game's Premium Edition upgrade.

That's according to new estimates from Alinea Analytics' Rhys Elliott, which reports Xbox has sold around 230,000 copies of Gears of War: E-Day since the prequel's advance-access release at the very beginning of the month - with 168,000 of those sales coming from Steam and 62,000 coming from Xbox consoles and PC.

Game Pass seemingly affected those stats to a large extent, like many other Xbox-published games this generation. Around 1.7m Locust-grinders played the shooter through their Game Pass subscription and more than 722,000 of them also bought the game's $30 Premium Edition upgrade.

You see, owners of the Premium Edition that costs $99.99 were allowed to fend off the hordes early - from the 1st of October - but Game Pass subscribers could and still can drop a cheaper $30 for the Premium Edition upgrade and all its add-on extras. E-Day then launched in full for regular Game Pass subscribers and Standard Edition buyers on 6th October.

When you include pure sales, microtransactions and those Premium Edition upgrades, Gears of War: E-Day has seemingly made above $37m (about £28). As Alinea noted, almost a million people paid something for E-Day.

"In a world without day-one Game Pass, many of these folks would have bought E-Day at $70," the analyst speculated. "They paid $30 for five days early access to something they don't own. Xbox is, in effect, charging its most valuable customers the least, based on a hangover from a tried-and-exhausted strategy from a previous administration."

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has already stopped new Call of Duty games from launching directly into the subscription service. With so much change afoot, it's not hard to imagine blockbuster games like Gears of War or Forza following suit.

Another interesting tidbit comes from player overlap. On Xbox, more than 80% of E-Day players previously tried another Gears game, Call of Duty, Fortnite, GTA 5 and Halo Infinite. On Steam, 72% of players came from Counter-Strike and 65% of folks came from Helldivers 2, which is probably unsurprising when you think about how similar E-Day's Horde Siege mode is to Arrowhead's PvE smash hit. Both have wide-open maps pulling you in all directions for side objectives and bug-like aliens to tear into chunks.

The Coalition studio head Mike Crump recently claimed that E-Day is a "great foundation" for future sequels, and promised the next Gears won't "take nearly as long" to make after the seven-year gap between entries. With the game fully emerged, all eyes now turn to The Coalition - several people at the studio spoke to Eurogamer and feared post-launch layoffs could be on the horizon.

"Gears of War: E-Day is a game of contrasts: conservative by its very nature, but with enough technical proficiency and iterative thinking to make its old-fashioned ideas feel competent and engaging," Eurogamer's Gears of War: E-Day review said. "Bleeding edge graphics with 20-year-old design sensibilities drip into this bloody crucible of familiarity that does nostalgia right."

articles.headline: Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar review: A great home theater option all by itself
keyFacts: The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar is a $1,099 home theater speaker featuring nine internal drivers and a glass-topped design.
Reviewers found that the soundbar provides enough low-end bass that users in small to medium spaces do not need an additional subwoofer.
Bose offers optional add-ons including a $349 rear speaker and an $899 subwoofer to expand the home theater system.
body: Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar review: A great home theater option all by itself
You won’t feel the need to immediately add a subwoofer to this one.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

When Bose proclaimed that the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar was its "loudest, deepest and most immersive" model yet, I still assumed it would need a subwoofer." Yet when I first connected the company's latest soundbar to my TV, I quickly realized it didn't need the extra bass boost. The combination of CleanBass tech and QuietPort acoustics provide enough low-end tone that you aren't likely to crave an additional, pricey sub. Since the soundbar alone is already $1,099, that was a welcome surprise.
Design

I get it: There's not a ton of room for innovation when it comes to the design of soundbars. They all have to be elongated and rectangular to be able to contain a collection of drivers without blocking your TV. But there is room for improvement when it comes to the general look of soundbars, and that's where Bose stepped up its game on the Lifestyle Ultra.

The speaker is short and wide, just like you'd expect, but the textured, knit-fabric grille elevates the overall aesthetic. This is more apparent on the white colorway than the black, and luckily the lighter color is exactly what was sent to me for review. Bose also opted for a glass top where the competition typically uses a plastic panel or just buttons. The glass portion doesn't extend all the way to the edges though, so there's room for the up-firing drivers to do their thing.

Another excellent design choice was the volume controls. Bose installed a touch-enabled, circular panel that allows you to spin your finger clockwise and counterclockwise to raise and lower the volume. You can also just tap the "+" or "-" if you'd rather. There's an area in the middle of the circle that you can tap to play, pause or skip tracks, as well as touch-based controls for Bluetooth, disabling the soundbar's microphone and summoning Alexa. All of that is positioned on the right side of the glass panel.

Inside, Bose arranged a collection of nine drivers for the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar's acoustic architecture. There are six full-range drivers, two of which are up-firing and the other four are front facing. Additionally, a center-mounted tweeter assists with dialogue clarity, while two so-called PhaseGuide drivers spread sound horizontally. To calibrate all of that for your living room, Bose's CustomTune feature uses the microphone in your Android or iOS device to analyze the space (speaker layout, surfaces and seating) and optimize the soundbar's output.

Like most soundbars these days, the Lifestyle Ultra only has a single HDMI eARC input. This isn't a problem per se, but if you need HDMI 2.0 passthrough for things like game consoles, just note that it's not available here.
In-use: Movies and music on the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar

The Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar is very much a plug-and-play device. Once you connect it to power and your TV, it's ready to go. However, you'll want to download the Bose app and run the CustomTune audio calibration ASAP to tailor the soundbar's output to the acoustics of your living room or home theater space. Of course, if you add either the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer or Lifestyle Ultra Speakers to the soundbar, you'll need to repeat the CustomTune process.

Once all of that is complete, the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar provides a solid boost to your TV audio. The up-firing and PhaseGuide drivers offer a pleasant level of immersion and dimensional audio, which is apparent on shows like Drive to Survive and Masters of the Air. The bass output is the most impressive thing about this soundbar, though. It's enough that users in small to medium spaces likely won't immediately feel the need to add a subwoofer. Even after several weeks of testing, I'm still baffled by the low-end performance when a sound effect demands that portion of the frequency range.

This bass is abundantly apparent for music, too. Sylvan Esso's "Flood Season" has ample lows for the bass guitar riffs and kick drum, while more bass-heavy tracks, like Russian Circles' "Empath," maintain the tonal depth without getting muddy. I also appreciate how the center tweeter allows vocals to consistently float on top of the mix. This makes albums like Hayley Williams' Ego Death At A Bachelorette Party particularly enjoyable.

As I already mentioned, Bose allows you to expand your home theater system with the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer and Lifestyle Ultra Speakers. Unless you have a larger space, or just crave the extra immersion that rear speakers can provide when watching movies or TV shows, I don't think either are absolutely necessary here.

The speakers are $349 each and the sub comes in at $899, but if you opt for the Home Theater Set or Surround Sound Set (Lifestyle Ultra bundles), you can save a few hundred dollars. (Oddly, Bose doesn't offer savings on the Extra Bass Set, which is the soundbar and subwoofer).

I tested the add-ons one at a time. First, I added the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer to the soundbar — perhaps the most likely additional purchase for most people. This achieves the obvious result of adding more bass, which could be preferential if you plan for the Lifestyle Ultra gear to pull double duty as your main music setup. But even in my living room, which is open to the main dining area and kitchen, the soundbar alone was still adequate for music.

I then added two Lifestyle Ultra Speakers as rear units, which I quickly discovered would be my preferred way to bolster the soundbar's performance. Since the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar holds its own in the bass department, its only true deficiency is directional audio and overall immersion. Add those two speakers to the rear and that weakness is fixed, and disabling the subwoofer doesn't result in much sacrifice to overall output. I only really noticed a big difference in certain scenes with really booming effects, like certain parts of the first episode of Masters of the Air (no spoilers from me).

AirPlay, Google Cast and Spotify Connect are all available on the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar for quick and easy music streaming. You can also opt for Bluetooth, if you prefer, but I find the three methods I mentioned are more convenient for getting audio from a phone or laptop to a soundbar.
The competition

The Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar does well enough on its own that Bose's primary competition is other companies that claim they've built all-in-one TV speakers that don't need a separate subwoofer. My top pick in that category is Samsung's QS90H, which costs $99 less at full price. This 7.1.2-channel soundbar not only provides adequate bass without a sub, but it has Samsung's Convertible Fit tech that allows you to place it flat or mounted upright. Sensors in the soundbar then reconfigure the output based on how it's sitting. Samsung included lots of other features, but some of them, like Q-Symphony, require a recent Samsung TV to use.

Another excellent option for a true all-in-one soundbar is the Sonos Arc Ultra. The company's flagship model is equipped with Sound Motion technology that handles the bass in a 9.1.4-channel setup. That last number indicates two additional height channels compared to the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar and the QS90H. The Arc Ultra not only has more channels overall, but it also contains more drivers than either the Bose or Samsung options, with 14 of those total. At full price, the Arc Ultra costs the same as the Lifestyle Ultra, but Sonos currently has it on sale for $899.
Editor's note: Bose is offering a $200 discount on the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar through October 11.
Wrap-up

Perhaps Bose's hesitance to label the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar as an all-in-one unit comes down to sales. I'm sure the company would prefer for you to buy the pricey subwoofer for a speaker combo that's common to living rooms. I'd recommend spending extra money on a pair of Lifestyle Ultra Speakers instead, and configure your home theater for better immersion rather than overly booming bass.

No matter what you choose, it won't change the fact that the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar can function as a standalone option to boost your TV sound. Plus, it's more than capable of double duty for music and the company offers all the standard features you'd expect in a flagship soundbar these days. Bose has built a worthy competitor to the likes of Samsung, Sonos and Sony here, so the only real question is which company's mix of hardware and features you prefer.

articles.headline: ‘I use AI to do the things that I’m bad at’: Linus Torvalds on why it works for him
keyFacts: Linux creator Linus Torvalds stated at Open Source Summit Europe that he enjoys using artificial intelligence for personal projects and tasks he dislikes.
Torvalds noted that while artificial intelligence tools help find and fix Linux kernel bugs, they also stress out maintainers with low-quality submissions.
Torvalds discussed how the Linux development process evolved over 35 years from manual patches to distributed version control systems like Git.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- Torvalds likes AI for showing new developers the joy of programming.
- Torvalds discussed changes in the Linux kernel development process.
- AI has become a vital component in finding and fixing bugs in the Linux kernel.

PRAGUE – Many open-source developers still dislike AI. The latest example is System76 banning AI-generated content from its COSMIC desktop. At Open Source Summit Europe, Linux creator Linus Torvalds offered a different take: “I actually really like using AI,” Torvald told Dirk Hohndel, his good friend and head of Ericsson Software Technology, in their latest discussion.
Also: 5 reasons why Linux will dominate desktop computing

But that enthusiasm comes with a distinction worth keeping in mind. Using AI to make a hobby project more enjoyable is one thing. Using it responsibly in the Linux kernel, where generated patches and bug reports can overwhelm maintainers, is another.
More from ZDNET
Torvalds said, “I think that you need to be very careful using AI when you’re doing something real and important.”
Torvalds likes AI, especially for beginners

“To be fair,” he continued, “I don’t do a lot of kernel programming. I’m a maintainer. The Linux kernel is a project where other people do the real work, and I act as the collection point. But I still enjoy programming immensely. I think AI is a wonderful tool if you use it correctly and treat it as a tool, and I find it makes programming much more enjoyable.”

Torvalds recalled, “I started programming in 1981 or so, and back then computers were much simpler, and you could understand what they were doing, and also the programs you compared your own programs to were much simpler.”
Also: The 6 AI-free Linux distros I recommend most

“It’s a different story today,” Torvalds said. “The bar in software engineering has grown so high that it’s hard to see your own small efforts as worth anything, because you’re used to all these polished, professional programs. “

“A lot of people make fun of vibe coding, but I think it’s a wonderful way to find joy in programming. It makes you feel like you’re doing something relevant. It allows you, as a new programmer, to do things that you would otherwise have a really hard time with.”

He continued: “I love the concept of AI as a gateway drug because I was working on my own toy project, the guitar pedal, and I knew what I was doing. I had a user interface that I had written myself in C that was running on a microcontroller that was running on this small screen, and I was like, “This is just stupid. It looks like something from the ’80s; I wanted it to look like something from this century. But I don’t do Java. I do kernels.”
Also: My 5 favorite Linux distros for security

“So, I use AI to do the things that I’m bad at,” Torvalds went on, “I’d seen all the same YouTube videos you have. Give AI a prompt, and it will do it. So I gave it a prompt, and it did it, and it was horrendous. Then I said, ‘Hey, look! I already did this in C. I did it the right way. It’s just ugly.”
AI in the Linux kernel

That’s not to say AI isn’t useful for finding and fixing mistakes in the Linux kernel. Hohndel asked about Sashiko, an agentic Linux kernel code review system. Torvalds said its public reviews now appear on the Linux Kernel Mailing List (LKML). Indeed, some subsystem maintainers now expect patches to have received such a review before accepting them.
That doesn’t mean all pull requests have to go through an AI review. Some maintainers do require it, though, and it seems likely that all will eventually require it.

AI tools can identify genuine security problems. They can also surface issues in old, no-longer-used drivers that have gone unnoticed for years. Torvalds sees value in the resulting fixes, while acknowledging their cost. “It is, I think, improving our code base… Although it is also stressing maintainers out to the point that it’s a problem.”

As Torvalds said in Mumbai earlier this year. convincing but fabricated bug reports can require substantial human effort to disprove, while narrowly targeted patches may fix one symptom without addressing the underlying problem. Torvalds called some submissions “mindless band-aid kind of patches.”

That said, AI code checking is here, and it’s here to stay. For example, Torvalds said, “three-quarters of the preceding day’s Linux Kernel Maintainer Summit discussion concerned making AI generation and review less stressful and more useful. The bottleneck isn’t getting patches. It’s getting useful work through review without exhausting the people responsible for it.
‘Me, myself, and my computer’

Because it was Linux’s 35th anniversary, Torvalds also talked about how the process of making Linux has changed over the years. In the beginning, Linux had no development infrastructure at all to speak of. Instead, Torvalds tracked changes through tarball patches and regularly distributed updated source code.
“I made patches every single day internally, and I released them at least weekly,” he recalled. “And it actually worked surprisingly well for a small project.”

Hohndel noted that the distribution of new tarballs and their accompanying changes continued until 2002, when Linux had become a much larger undertaking. Back in those days, Torvalds said, “It was really just me, myself, and my computer.”

His reluctance to adopt existing source-control tools was not simply stubbornness. He wanted developers to work independently, with their own local environments. “I really felt very strongly that everybody should have their own local setup,” he said.

As I explained in my 2025 account of Linux’s growth, drawing on Jonathan Corbet’s history of the project, Linux’s openness attracted an expanding development community. But relying on Torvalds to apply incoming patches manually became a bottleneck. Accepting contributions by hand was no longer enough; the project needed a better way to integrate them.
BitKeeper was controversial – and useful

The BitKeeper version control system provided that improvement, although its proprietary licensing divided the kernel community. Some developers refused to use it. Torvalds, however, found that distributed source control made it substantially easier to merge work from subsystems such as networking and ARM. Torvalds said, “BitKeeper, as far as I’m concerned, was a huge success.”
He didn’t consider it flawless. Rather, it showed him what source control could do and helped him identify what he actually wanted. Nor did its adoption require every maintainer to use the same tool.

Then the 2005 BitKeeper licensing dispute took away the tool he had come to depend on. After experiencing distributed source control, returning to the old approach was no longer appealing. Git was Torvalds’ answer.

Hohndel recalled that Torvalds took 11 days to produce the first working version: a new object model, code, and a functioning tool in under two weeks. The early Git was not universally popular. Developers accustomed to CVS found it unfamiliar, and its first versions had rough edges.

Its eventual success still surprises Torvalds. Today, according to a 2022 Stack Overflow Developer survey, Git has become the de facto standard for version control: Nearly 94% of respondents, and almost 97% of professional developers, use Git. All Torvalds wanted was a tool for Linux, not to remake software development everywhere. As he put it, “I sometimes get way too much credit for Git.”

After roughly six months, he handed over its maintenance. His point was that the subsequent decades of development belonged to other people, not that the initial work was unimportant. “It’s worth noting that Git today is a lot better than Git in 2005.”
The kernel should improve without becoming exciting
Linux’s release process underwent another major change, moving away from long-lived, separate stable and development trees toward frequent releases, a merge window, and release candidates.

Under the older model, work accumulated in the development tree while distributions backported desired changes into stable kernels. Releases intended to happen annually could stretch into years, making planning difficult. Torvalds proposed a dramatically shorter cycle. The reaction was not enthusiastic. “People looked at me like I had grown a third head.”
Also: Even Linus Torvalds is vibe coding now

His initial five-week target was intentionally aggressive. The process ultimately settled into the familiar nine-to-ten-week rhythm. The result is a development model Torvalds still finds remarkably effective. “We now, for the last 20 years, have a really stable, working model.”

He also rejected the idea that Linux should organize itself around dramatic feature launches. “I’m a big believer in the whole incremental small changes that, over time, turn into big features.” As he had said this summer in Mumbai, Linux’s development goal remains “incremental improvement and steady progress all the time.”
So, while AI is changing Linux’s problem-finding and fixing mechanisms, the name of the game for Linux remains rapid, small improvements to an essential, stable operating system.
